liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (4 reviews): Reviewer calls the jam great, a somewhat tarnished gem worth sitting through the show for; Probably the best-played version of 1995, arriving as a surprise after about half an hour of sleepy Garcia [11][14][15][18]
- **Touch of Grey** (1 review): Jerry forgot much of the lyrics at the start of the opener [11]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Contains some of the best jamming the reviewer has heard from 1995 [15]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Nice jam between Truckin' and Terrapin, with Spanish hints [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **Long Way to Go**: rare: 3 archived performances [20]
- **I Want to Tell You**: rare: 7 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1995-05-24.pzm.russjcan.97610.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 155 min [1]
- **gd1995-05-24.partial.sbd.larson.35181.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 7 songs; 74 min; rated 2.17/5 by 6 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the soundboard sounds definitely great; Reviewer says the soundboard sounds great [13][17]
- **gd95-05-24.neumann.18800.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 158 min; rated 2.33/5 by 8 [2]
- **gd1995-05-24.nuemannKM140.unknown.larson.35153.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 158 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- Concert had serious impact on downtown; buses took over parking lots usually used by workers for three days [1]
- Second set ran 98 minutes from I Want To Tell You through Lovelight, with U.S. Blues as encore [2]
- Soundcheck is included, featuring Tough Mama, Unbroken Chain into Childhood's End and back, and Rain [4]
- Reviewer's first 1995 show; watched with fascinated horror, having previously heard only the Salt Lake show [10]
- Reviewer's first time out west since the New Year run of 91-92; enjoyed the scene with friends from Canada [12]
- Reviewer finds this show no better or worse than other 1995 shows, and dislikes them [9]
- Reviewer says these Seattle shows were better than the Oregon shows right afterward [12]
- Reviewer prefers the first Estimated Prophet, from 2-26-77, over later versions like this one [13]
- Reviewer says it was the only part of the show, or the whole run, that nearly shone [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1995-05-24.pzm.russjcan.97610.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Russ Cansler; transferred by Russ Cansler; source: Hat mounted Realistic pzm's > Sony WMD6-C, 60ft, dfc MAC>NakCR-3A>HD>Audacity>CDWave>TLH [1]. Also: This copy omits Bob saying they'd be back shortly at the end of the first set [1]
- **gd1995-05-24.partial.sbd.larson.35181.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Chris Larson; source: unknown sbd (GDHour?) > dat [6]. Also: Soundboard may come from the gdhour; uploader unsure whether it's from the FM broadcast or an unbroadcast source [6]
- **gd95-05-24.neumann.18800.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Ross M. and Chris Larson; source: Audience: Neumann KM140's [2]
- **gd1995-05-24.nuemannKM140.unknown.larson.35153.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Chris Larson; source: Af:Nueman KM140>DAT(48kHz) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1995-05-25 Memorial Stadium, Seattle, WA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1995-05-25-memorial-stadium-seattle-wa-usa/) [21]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Seattle Center Memorial Stadium - May 24, 1995](https://www.dead.net/show/may-24-1995) [22]
